solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 5 down, corrected here

entries.clue: Cleans clothing for performer in theatre (6)

blocks.note: a verb: cleans hard with a brush
the loose uniform a surgeon wears in the operating theatre

annotation.surface: An actor's costume goes off to be laundered.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage, so the 'performer' is a surgeon at work.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the verb for hard cleaning, and the noun for hospital operating wear.

entries.clue: Mexican sauce one thrifty daughter secured in deal (5,5)

indicators.note: something secured in a place is held fast inside it, so these pieces sit inside the deal

blocks.note: a deal on price, a sale
one who is thrifty is a saver

annotation.surface: A careful shopper gets the sauce cheap in a sale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One thrifty' is a single piece, a person who is thrifty, not I or A plus a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: salsa verde, green sauce, is a staple of Mexican cooking.

entries.clue: Right fashion to do away with top villain (5)

indicators.note: to do away with the top of a word is to kill off its first letter

blocks.note: VOGUE, fashion, without its first letter V

annotation.surface: A villain plots the right way to assassinate a leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To do away with top' reads as murder in the surface, fitting a villain, but it only beheads the fashion word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a villain.

entries.clue: In general, minor route empty lately (7)

indicators.note: an empty word has had its contents removed, leaving just the outer shell

blocks.note: a B-road, a minor road in Britain

annotation.surface: A remark that country lanes have been quiet recently.
annotation.walkthrough: British roads are graded: A-roads are main routes, B-roads the minor ones. 'Empty' looks like it describes the road but acts on the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'broadly speaking' and 'in general' both mean without going into detail.

entries.clue: Going along with engineers getting on ferries (8)

indicators.note: to ferry is to carry across, so one word carries the other inside it

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps

annotation.surface: Army engineers boarding ferries as they go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' reads as boarding a boat; here it means growing old.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to go along with a plan is to agree with it.

entries.clue: Character boringly photographs sandwiches (5)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer between its outer parts, like a filling between slices

blocks.note: the letters run across the word break, after BORIN and before OTOGRAPHS

annotation.surface: A dull person who takes pictures of their lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person in the surface but means a written symbol; GLYPH straddles the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a character in writing, especially a carved or stylised one, is a glyph.

entries.clue: Runner starts to extend strides and head east (7)

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Extend and Strides

annotation.surface: Coaching for a sprinter: lengthen your stride and set off eastward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a verb in the surface but is a noun here: a promontory.
annotation.definitionFit: A runner in the sense of a fugitive: someone who has got out and is on the run.

entries.clue: Showed dedication forgetting nothing that’s arranged (9)

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so the letter goes
letters that are arranged are put into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone showed commitment by dropping everything that had been planned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Showed dedication' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Showed', and 'dedication' is the raw material.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to indicate something is to show or point it out.

entries.clue: European wanting a new beginning (4)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word goes without the letters that follow

annotation.surface: A European longing for a fresh start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' is a noun here, as in the germ of an idea, not the verb it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: The germ of an idea is its seed or first beginning.

entries.clue: Wonderful rising throw is hard to grasp (8)

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word that rises is read from the bottom up, so backwards

annotation.surface: A great high throw that's tricky to catch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard to grasp' pretends to be about catching the ball; it means difficult to understand.
annotation.definitionFit: Something baffling is puzzling, beyond one's mental grasp.

entries.clue: Soldier on island track (9)

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

annotation.surface: A soldier posted to an island railway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a preposition but is a cricket term: the leg side of the field is also the on side.
annotation.definitionFit: A Roman foot soldier, one who served in a legion; the clue uses the plain sense.

entries.clue: Wood part taken back from trade customer (5)

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the phrase that follows
something taken back goes the other way, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the break, after T and before USTOMER

annotation.surface: A timber merchant accepts a return from a trade buyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken back' reads as a returned purchase; it tells you to read the hidden letters in reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cedar is one kind of wood.

entries.clue: Advanced Scout Leader more successful than others (5,2,3,4)

blocks.note: A = advanced, as in A level
Cub Scouts are organised in packs, each with its own leader

annotation.surface: A senior scout leader who outshines the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advanced Scout Leader' reads as one rank; 'Advanced' splits off as a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from racing: runners ahead of the pack are beating the rest.

entries.clue: Stand to cut salad plant showing no sign of bending? (10)

indicators.note: one word cuts into the other, slicing it open

blocks.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

annotation.surface: Instructions for chopping a salad plant that won't wilt.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a fold leaves a crease, so an unbent thing has none.
annotation.definitionFit: A fold or bend leaves a crease, so something never bent is free of creases.

entries.clue: One’s written extreme letters to Santa, we’re told (5)

definitions.note: 'One's written' means 'one that is written', a noun.

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters
what we are told we hear, so the result is spoken, not read

blocks.note: Santa's end letters are S and A, said as letter names

annotation.surface: A child's letter to Father Christmas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters to Santa' pretends to be a Christmas list; the letters are literal ones, S and A.
annotation.definitionFit: Read as 'one that is written': an essay is a piece of writing.

entries.clue: Reduction in size as gherkin gets pickled (9)

indicators.note: pickled means drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: A cucumber shrinks in the jar as it is pickled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true, since gherkins do shrink in brine, which hides the anagram well.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: shrinkage is the amount by which something gets smaller.

entries.clue: Officer directed ten cops with tips from informer (9)

indicators.note: letters that are directed are steered into a new order
the tips of a word are its two ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of Informer

annotation.surface: A police officer in charge of ten constables, acting on a tip-off from a grass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips from informer' reads as tip-offs from a grass; the tips are the end letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an inspector is a rank of police officer.

entries.clue: Boat bearing king’s flag (8)

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the boat carries the king inside it

annotation.surface: A ship flying the royal standard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King's flag' reads as one royal banner; the apostrophe-s is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

entries.clue: Shooter no good behind short fences (9)

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter
to fence something is to enclose it, so the word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: DERRIERE, a behind, missing its last letter

annotation.surface: A useless marksman lurking behind low fences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun, a bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for a gun: a shooter, and a derringer is a small pocket pistol.

entries.clue: I would ultimately love partner in a perfect world (7)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the word's final letter

annotation.surface: A wistful wish to find love and a partner in some ideal world.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence of longing, which hides that the definition is its last four words.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiomatic equivalent: 'ideally' and 'in a perfect world' both introduce the best case.

entries.clue: Very small car carrying case of old alcohol (5)

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the outer pieces hold the inner one
the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the Ford Ka, a small car

annotation.surface: A tiny car smuggling an old crate of spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very small' reads as one phrase but splits: V for very, then the small car.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: vodka is one kind of alcoholic spirit.

entries.clue: Man taking wine and bread from France (7)

indicators.note: it tells you the words are to be taken in French

blocks.note: bread is slang for money; a cent is a coin of the euro, France's currency

annotation.surface: A man bringing back wine and a loaf from France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From France' applies to both pieces; 'bread' is money, not a loaf.
annotation.definitionFit: A man's first name, the crossword convention for defining a name by 'man'.

entries.clue: Unstoppable rebellion near Bali at sea (14)

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

annotation.surface: An unstoppable uprising just off the Indonesian coast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the island setting so neatly that it passes for a location rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what cannot be restrained cannot be stopped.

entries.clue: Giant bird wings in action (5)

indicators.note: a word's wings are its two sides, the outermost letters

blocks.note: a tit is a small bird

annotation.surface: A huge bird in flight, wings working.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Giant bird' reads as one phrase; the joke is that the bird here is tiny.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek myth: the Titans were a race of giants, so any giant is a titan.

entries.clue: Poor man’s dismal in the end being replaced by Romeo (5)

indicators.note: what comes in the end is the word's final letter
a replaced letter is swapped out for the one that follows

blocks.note: bloke, British slang for a man
last letter of dismaL, swapped out
Romeo = R in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A poor fellow's gloom lifts at last when Romeo turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor man' reads as one phrase; 'Poor' alone is the definition and the 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: to be broke is to have no money, to be poor.

entries.clue: Select prime locations in Bearsden for facility (4)

indicators.note: prime locations are positions numbered by prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7

blocks.note: letters 2, 3, 5 and 7 of the town name

annotation.surface: Choosing sites in Bearsden, a town near Glasgow, for a new amenity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' sounds like estate-agent talk but means prime-numbered positions; 'facility' sounds like a building.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something with facility means doing it with ease.

entries.clue: Benefit of a face covering reported (5)

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.surface: Asking what good a face mask does.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Benefit of' reads like a question about masks; 'of' only links definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: As in 'to no avail': avail is use or benefit.

entries.clue: So rushed to acquire present by first of February (9)

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so the word takes the other pieces inside it
by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: here = present, as in a roll call

annotation.surface: Someone hurried out to buy a gift before February began.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, the obvious reading after 'rushed to acquire'; it means in attendance.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'so' and 'therefore' both introduce a consequence.

entries.clue: All night before event English greyhound regularly feeds (8)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter
to feed is to put something in, so these letters go inside the others

blocks.note: the eve is the night before

annotation.surface: A dog-racing tip: the English greyhound eats well the night before the event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feeds' reads as the greyhound eating; it tells you to put the letters inside EVE plus E.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'all' and 'everyone' both mean every person present.

entries.clue: Different people turning to that woman and son (6)

indicators.note: a word turning round faces the other way, so read it backwards

annotation.surface: A mother and son who have become different people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Different people turning' reads as people changing; 'turning' works only on the tiny word 'to'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'others' means people other than those already named.
